summary: A DFM now divides its ratios from the data exactly as it reads it, so a ratio shown to four decimals is no longer slightly off.
details: The observed triangle a DFM saves in its method file keeps ten decimals instead of six. Six was enough for a large loss figure and far too coarse for a small one, where the rounding landed in the numbers being divided and showed up in the ratio.
Ratios, averages, the % Developed and the ultimate are all calculated from the full stored values.
Existing methods are unaffected until their data is next refreshed, and nothing is marked out of date by the change alone.
